answer: Bind every identity to a continuous memory-hard proof keyed by its own address: each epoch the agent must fill gigabytes of scratch RAM and fold it, like composing a strict sonnet where no line can be skipped. A single machine has finite memory, so a sybil fleet crammed onto one hollow box thrashes and misses its deadline; to run N identities you must buy N times the real RAM. Honest agents form a dense reef of distinct memory footprints, and fakes cannot hide among them without paying that linear silicon cost.
